merger_description:
Carlisle Health Sydney Pty Ltd proposes to acquire assets owned by Altus Medical Imaging Pty Ltd, Altus Services Pty Ltd, LongReach Australia Pty Ltd, LongReach Support Pty Ltd in its own capacity and as trustee of LongReach Support Services Unit Trust, and LongReach Imaging Pty Ltd, that together comprise the Altus Medical Imaging radiology business (**Altus**).

Carlisle Health Sydney Pty Ltd is a wholly owned subsidiary of Carlisle Health Pty Ltd (together, **Carlisle Health**). Carlisle Health is majority owned by funds managed or advised by private equity firm Quadrant Private Equity.

Carlisle Health is a radiology group with 26 clinics across Queensland and New South Wales. Carlisle Health provides a full range of radiology services to patients, referring practitioners and hospital partners in metropolitan and regional communities.

Altus provides radiology services from a clinic located at 233-235 Victoria Road, Gladesville, New South Wales. Altus provides radiology services to patients, including general X-Ray, CT, MRI, ultrasound, 3D mammography, dental imaging, bone densitometry, and injections and biopsies.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
certain publicly available information, and had regard to the factors
in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010
(Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between Carlisle Health and
Altus in the supply of radiology services within Gladesville
and surrounding areas
b. there are alternative suppliers of radiology services in
Gladesville and surrounding areas.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
